title: Atlas service account access token in a Bearer header
summary: A synthetic access token after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header of a request to the Atlas Administration API, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map.
rationale: Atlas documents the token it issues at the OAuth token endpoint as a Bearer token sent in the Authorization header, valid for 1 hour. The documentation states no prefix, alphabet or width for it, so the scheme in the carrier is the only identifying context and no bare-value rule is implied. The Bearer scheme is generic, so the attribution stays generic; the extent is the value after the scheme and excludes the closing quote.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after an explicit Bearer scheme in an Authorization header of an Atlas Administration API request is treated as a credential and covered whole. Atlas documents the Bearer carrier and the 1 hour lifetime (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic authorization attribution are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: info.description: 'returns a Bearer token that is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds)'

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
